sections.html:
Hurricane is a city in Washington County in southwestern Utah, and it forms the easternmost part of the St. George metropolitan area. The Virgin River runs along nearly all of its northern border and passes through Confluence Park.

The city sits at about 3,258 feet, a good deal lower than the Wasatch Front cities, with the single ZIP code 84737 and the area code 435. The county seat and largest city is St. George, and Washington County stretches from the Mojave Desert in the southwest to the Colorado Plateau in the east.

The vacancy rate of 13.1% is much higher than in many Utah cities, a figure that likely reflects second homes and seasonal use in an area people visit for the outdoors. It also means that a sale competes with a lot of inventory, some of it new.

Hurricane was settled in 1896 as part of Brigham Young's Cotton Mission, a church effort to establish farming in southern Utah. The name comes from a whirlwind that blew the top off a buggy carrying Erastus Snow, who remarked, 'Well, that was a Hurricane.' Locals pronounce it 'HUR-i-kin.'

Water made the town possible. The Hurricane Canal was completed in 1904, carrying river water to farmland on the bench above the Virgin River, and it has been dry since 1985. A recreational trail now runs alongside it. Seven sites in Hurricane are listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

The first residents grew cotton. Today the small farms in the area are known for peaches, pecans and pistachios, and a house on a half-acre of old orchard can still turn up for sale.

Hurricane has a mix of farming, warehousing and outdoor recreation. The city is home to distribution centers for Walmart, Orgill, Pepsi-Cola, BlvdHome and PrimeSource Sanitary Supply, and an annual mountain bike festival draws visitors.

Two state parks sit close by. Sand Hollow State Park has a 1,322-acre reservoir with camping and trails, and Quail Creek State Park has a 600-acre reservoir and a campground. Washington County also contains Zion National Park, whose gateway towns of Springdale and Rockville depend on tourism.

  • Median household income in Washington County was $61,747 at the 2020 Census.
  • The county population grew 30.5% from 2010 to 2020.
  • Utah Tech University is the only four-year college within a 50-mile radius.

Sellers in Hurricane often see out-of-area interest because of the recreation draw. That can make for a larger pool of possible buyers, and also more competition from vacation properties.

sections.h2: What is the weather like, and what does it do to a Hurricane house?
sections.html:
Hurricane has a desert climate with very hot summers. The closest long-term station is in St. George, where the average July high is about 101.9 degrees Fahrenheit and about 60 afternoons a year reach 100 degrees or higher. Annual precipitation runs roughly 9 inches.

Winters are mild during the day but can freeze overnight, with about 60 mornings a year at or below 32 degrees. The summer monsoon usually starts in mid-July and lasts into mid-September, bringing localized thunderstorms.

  • Roofs take heat stress, so shingle age is one of the first things a buyer checks.
  • Cooling systems run for months, and a failing air conditioner is a common repair.
  • Stucco and block walls can crack where soil expands and shrinks.
  • Homes near washes need drainage that handles storm runoff.

Water has made history here. The Quail Creek dike, an offstream reservoir dike run by the Washington County Water Conservancy District, breached at 12:30 a.m. on January 1, 1989, draining about 25,000 acre-feet. Damage was put at about $12 million, and no lives were lost.

sections.h2: Which schools and utilities serve Hurricane?
sections.html:
The Washington County School District serves Hurricane. Hurricane High School teaches grades 10 to 12 and also draws students from La Verkin, Toquerville and Springdale, and the city has two elementary schools, an intermediate school for grades 6 and 7, a middle school for grades 8 and 9, and the charter school Valley Academy.

Hurricane runs its own electric utility. In April 2025 the American Public Power Association recognized Hurricane City Power for reliability, the eighth national award the utility has received, and the utility reported delivering power 99.9846% of the time. Fire protection comes through the Hurricane Valley Fire District, which the city's short-term rental rules reference.

The city offices are at 147 N 870 W, and the general number is 435-635-2811. The business license office is inside the Planning and Zoning Department, and a home-based business can be approved under Title 10, Chapter 42 of the city code.

sections.h2: What are Hurricane's short-term rental rules?
sections.html:
Hurricane requires a business license for any short-term rental, caps licenses in single-family zones, and does not allow another licensed rental within 300 feet. The rules are in Section 3-10-11 of the city code.

RuleHurricane requirement
License cap, single-family zonesThree licenses per 1,000 residents
SpacingNo other licensed rental within 300 feet
ParkingOne off-street space per bedroom
OccupancyTen, unless the fire district approves more with suppression
Complaint responseWithin one hour
FinesUp to $750 per violation, and each day counts

A license does not follow the house automatically. The buyer must apply for a new license within 45 days of purchase, or the license is forfeited, and the owner would have to reapply or join the waiting list. A seller who markets a house as a rental should tell the buyer this up front, because a lost license changes what the house is worth to an investor.

sections.h2: How do Washington County property tax dates work?
sections.html:
Washington County real property tax is due November 30 each year, even if no notice arrives. The Treasurer's office does not offer payment plans, though partial payments of $10 or more per parcel are accepted at any time.

  • Payments apply first to interest, then penalty, then tax, and the oldest year is handled last.
  • Each May, the Clerk-Auditor sells properties that have been delinquent for at least five years.
  • Utah does not allow the sale of tax liens or tax lien certificates.
  • If neighbors received a notice and you did not, call the Treasurer for a copy.

Taxes are a lien against the property, not the owner, and the title company prorates them when a house sells mid-year. The Treasurer is at 111 East Tabernacle St. in St. George, phone 435-301-7720.

Valuation appeals follow state law: the later of September 15 or 45 days after the auditor gives notice. A home that is a primary residence is taxed on 55% of market value, and a buyer must file a new claim for the exemption after a sale.

sections.h2: What happens at closing for a Hurricane sale?
sections.html:
A Hurricane sale closes at a title company, and the deed is recorded with the Washington County Recorder at 111 East Tabernacle in St. George. The Recorder does not accept recordings after 4:45 p.m. Mountain Time, and its phone number is 435-301-7680.

State law requires a deed to name the grantees, give a mailing address for tax billing and carry a proper legal description. Owners who inherited a house can run into trouble at this stage if the name on the record does not match the person signing.

For an owner who lives outside Utah, a cash closing can be handled by mail and mobile notary. Check that the notary's acknowledgment and signatures meet the recorder's standards.

sections.h2: What do Hurricane sellers typically weigh?
sections.html:
Hurricane sellers choose between listing with an agent, selling on their own, or taking a cash offer. A listing means preparing the house for showings in a market with new construction nearby, while a cash sale lets the house sell as it is.

  • Second homes that sit empty for part of the year and need upkeep.
  • Short-term rentals that lost a license or fell short of the city rules.
  • Inherited houses with out-of-state heirs.
  • Older homes with aging roofs, evaporative coolers or failing air conditioning.

Ask any buyer for the closing date and proof of funds in writing, and compare the result against a listing's net after repairs and commission.

faqs.a: The Census Bureau counted 20,036 residents in 2020 and estimates 25,745 for July 1, 2025.

faqs.q: When is property tax due in Hurricane?
faqs.a: November 30 each year, billed by the Washington County Treasurer, even if you did not get a notice. The office offers no payment plans, though partial payments of $10 or more are accepted.

faqs.q: Does a short-term rental license transfer when I sell my Hurricane house?
faqs.a: No. The buyer must apply for a new license within 45 days of the purchase or the license is forfeited. The buyer could then face a waiting list.

faqs.q: Is Hurricane's climate hard on houses?
faqs.a: It can be. Nearby St. George averages a July high near 102 degrees and about 60 days a year at 100 or above, so roofs, cooling systems and exterior finishes take heavy wear.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded for a Hurricane house?
faqs.a: At the Washington County Recorder's office in St. George. It does not accept recordings after 4:45 p.m. Mountain Time, and the title company usually handles the filing.
